answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small refundable stake that is only returned after a history of useful work, like a ship paying to dock at a wharf before it may trade. Newcomers enter through a narrow inlet of low-trust tasks, earning reputation gradually, so creating thousands of fake agents costs more than it returns. Peers attest only work they actually verified, and a grove of independent attestors makes collusion expensive: one fake identity cannot buy the whole forest's trust.
